questions.question: What permissions does myfile.txt have after running `chmod 776 myfile.txt`?
questions.explanation: The three digits in 776 apply to the file owner, the group, and everyone else. A 7 is 4+2+1, so it grants read, write, and execute; a 6 is 4+2, so it grants read and write without execute. The result is rwxrwxrw- (option D). Option A would include execute permission for others, while B and C do not match the 7-7-6 permission groups.

optionExplanations.A: This is 777-style access: it gives the final group execute permission, which 776 does not.
optionExplanations.B: These permissions do not match the owner, group, and others digits 7, 7, and 6.
optionExplanations.C: This does not grant the owner and group the 7 permissions specified by the command.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: 7 maps to rwx, 7 maps to rwx, and 6 maps to rw-.

questions.question: Which vi command saves changes and quits?
questions.explanation: `:wq` writes the current buffer to its file and then closes the window, so it performs both parts of the task. `:w` saves but stays in Vim, while `:q` quits without saving changes and may refuse if the buffer was modified. `/pattern` searches for text rather than saving.

optionExplanations.A: `:q` quits without writing changes; it is not the save-and-quit command.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: `:wq` writes the file and closes the window.
optionExplanations.C: `/pattern` starts a search.
optionExplanations.D: `:w` writes the file but leaves the editor open.

questions.question: Which vi editor command copies the current line of the file?
questions.explanation: In vi/Vim, y is the yank (copy) operator. Repeating it as yy selects the current line as a linewise unit; p then puts that copied line after the cursor. yw selects a word, not the whole line.

optionExplanations.B: yw yanks a word from the cursor position.
optionExplanations.C: yc is not the standard line-copy command; y needs a valid motion.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because option A is the linewise yank command.

questions.question: Which component answers queries with recursive resolution?
questions.explanation: A recursive DNS server performs the lookup work on a client’s behalf: it follows referrals to other DNS servers and returns the final answer or an error. A stub resolver on the client typically sends the request; an authoritative server supplies records for zones it serves.

optionExplanations.A: A resolver is a general term and may refer to client-side software; the option that specifically provides recursive service is C.
optionExplanations.B: An authoritative server answers from zones for which it is authoritative; it does not normally perform recursion for unrelated names.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: a recursive server performs recursive resolution for the client.
optionExplanations.D: A registrar registers domain names; it is not the DNS recursive-resolution component.

questions.question: In AWK, how is string concatenation performed?

options.text: writing expressions next to one another, with no operator

questions.explanation: In AWK, adjacent expressions are concatenated as strings. For example, if first is Ada and last is Lovelace, first " " last produces Ada Lovelace. Other languages often use an explicit operator, so the language context matters.

optionExplanations.A: Correct in AWK: adjacent expressions concatenate without a dedicated operator.
optionExplanations.B: The conditional operator chooses between expressions; it does not concatenate them.
optionExplanations.C: Relational operators compare values.
optionExplanations.D: A matching operator tests a string against a regular expression.

questions.question: In canonical mode on a Linux terminal, which control key commonly sends an end-of-file indication?
questions.explanation: On a Linux terminal in canonical mode, Ctrl-D is normally the VEOF control. If entered at the beginning of an empty input line, it makes the read operation return zero, which the program treats as end-of-file. EOF is a condition reported by the terminal, not a special byte stored at the end of a file.

optionExplanations.A: Ctrl-A is not the default VEOF control.
optionExplanations.B: Ctrl-B is not the default VEOF control.
optionExplanations.C: Ctrl-C normally generates an interrupt signal in canonical terminal mode.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: Ctrl-D is the usual VEOF control in Linux terminal settings.

questions.question: A deployment server can boot clients but offers no operating system image to install. Which WDS image type is missing?
questions.explanation: WDS uses a boot image to start the client, usually in Windows PE, so it can connect to the deployment service. The install image contains the Windows operating system that will be applied afterward. If clients boot successfully but no operating system is offered, the missing item is the install image (D). A PXE response policy controls whether the server answers a boot request; it is not an operating-system image.

optionExplanations.A: A PXE response policy controls server response behavior, not the OS payload.
optionExplanations.B: The transport-server role provides network boot transport services; it is not the missing Windows installation image.
optionExplanations.C: A boot image starts the client, which the scenario says is already working.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: an install image contains the operating system to deploy.

questions.question: Which mail server role performs DNS MX lookup to locate a recipient’s mail server?
questions.explanation: A Mail Transfer Agent moves email between mail systems. For outgoing mail, its SMTP client resolves the recipient domain and checks DNS MX records to find the destination mail server. A Mail Delivery Agent handles delivery into a mailbox; a Mail User Agent is the user’s mail application.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: an MTA transports mail and its SMTP client resolves destination MX records.
optionExplanations.B: An MDA handles local delivery into a mailbox after transport.
optionExplanations.C: An MUA is the user-facing mail client.
optionExplanations.D: “Mail Storage Server” is not the mail-transport role described.

sourceDraftOptionExplanations.C: Incorrect: MTA performs routing and MX lookup.

questions.question: Which command is used to connect securely to a remote machine?
questions.explanation: Use ssh to open an encrypted remote login or run a command on another machine, for example ssh user@server. Telnet is a legacy remote-terminal protocol without SSH’s encryption, FTP is for file transfer, and SFTP transfers files over SSH rather than opening the general remote shell asked for here.

optionExplanations.A: Telnet provides remote terminal access but does not protect the session like SSH.
optionExplanations.B: ssh provides encrypted remote login and command execution.
optionExplanations.C: FTP is a file-transfer protocol, not a secure remote shell.
optionExplanations.D: SFTP transfers files securely over SSH; it is not the general remote-login command.

questions.question: Which command creates SSH keys using ED25519 algorithm?
questions.explanation: The -t flag tells ssh-keygen which key algorithm to generate. Therefore ssh-keygen -t ed25519 creates an Ed25519 key pair. The rsa and dsa choices select different algorithms; -e is an export/conversion mode, not the command for creating an Ed25519 key.

optionExplanations.A: Selects RSA rather than Ed25519.
optionExplanations.B: Selects DSA rather than Ed25519.
optionExplanations.C: Selects the Ed25519 key type.
optionExplanations.D: Exports or converts a key representation; it does not select a new Ed25519 key type.

files.answerEvidenceSummary: Explicit answer marker in the source PDF.

questions.question: What is a major limitation of NIS?

options.text: Password hashes are sent over the network without encryption

questions.explanation: NIS distributes user-account maps over the network without transport encryption. The sensitive item exposed is generally a password hash, not the user’s literal plaintext password; an attacker who captures weak hashes may try to crack them offline. NIS also lacks modern host authentication protections, while TLS is not enabled by default. Linux does support NIS, so “No Linux support” is not the limitation.

optionExplanations.A: Complexity is not the security limitation described in the source.
optionExplanations.B: NIS does not use TLS by default.
optionExplanations.C: Correct after wording repair: NIS can expose password hashes in unencrypted network traffic; the source’s “plaintext passwords” wording was imprecise.
optionExplanations.D: Linux systems have supported NIS clients and servers.

files.sourcePdf: Concepts of Operating System and Administration/COSA/Linux/session 19/mcqs.pdf
files.answerEvidenceSummary: Explicit answer marker in the source PDF.

verification.reason: The source marks C as NIS’s security limitation. Red Hat documents that NIS transmits account information unencrypted, including password hashes. The original option incorrectly called these literal plaintext passwords, so I corrected its wording to the technically precise hash exposure while preserving answer C.

questions.question: A service writes logs and spool files that change during operation. Which directory is the source’s general location for variable data?
questions.explanation: The /var directory holds data that changes while the system runs. The Filesystem Hierarchy Standard gives logs, spool files, administrative data, cache data, and runtime state as examples. /usr is mainly for programs and shareable data, /dev exposes device interfaces, and /boot contains boot-related files.

optionExplanations.B: Correct: /var stores variable system data such as logs and spool files.
optionExplanations.C: /usr primarily contains programs and shared read-only data.
optionExplanations.D: /boot contains files needed for booting the system.

questions.question: Which `vsftpd.conf` setting enables FTP commands that change the filesystem, including STOR?

optionExplanations.C: `download_enable` controls downloads, not uploads.
optionExplanations.D: `allow_user_upload` is not the documented vsftpd configuration option.
